ucq_rotunda_walk.description: Deathguard Halloran has watched a hundred newly arrived dead wander into the Canal because they could not tell one quarter from another. The city is a wheel, he says, and the wheel does not forgive the lost. Walk the four great halls (Royal, Magic, War and Apothecarium) and learn the shape of it before it learns yours.
ucq_rotunda_walk.accept_text: Four quarters, one wheel. Royal to the north-west, Magic to the north-east, War to the south-west, Apothecarium to the south-east. Walk all four. Count the guards in each. If a guard counts you back, you are doing it right. The sewers are for people who do not listen.
ucq_rotunda_walk.turn_in_text: You came back and you are not green. The Undercity has a use for you yet. Most newcomers get as far as the first bridge and decide they would rather be elsewhere. I do not blame them. It is a great deal of dead for one place.

ucq_muster_slip.description: Halloran has a muster slip for Executor Wrenfall, who holds the Royal Quarter's north gate. Halloran cannot leave his post, and he does not trust the couriers. The Executor is touchy about her paperwork, and touchier about who touches it, so he would like it delivered without anyone reading it first.
ucq_muster_slip.accept_text: Along the north promenade, west of the elevator. The Executor will want it in her hand, not on her desk. If she asks what's in it, tell her you were not curious. She will like you for it, and will not believe you.
ucq_muster_slip.turn_in_text: Halloran. Of course. Never a word wasted. Here, take something for your troubles. And tell him next time to send the slip with a little more ink. I could read it from the other side of the room, which is a failing in a secret.

ucq_scarlet_pressure.description: Scarlet Zealots and Bowmen are patrolling the Tirisfal road to the Ruins, close enough to see the portal. Executor Wrenfall has no intention of finding out whether they are brave enough to try the gate. She wants them thinned before they decide to find out for her, and she will not ask how many you take.
ucq_scarlet_pressure.accept_text: The Scarlet Watch Post, east of Brill. Zealots and bowmen, eight and six. Leave none in sight of the road. They shout scripture when they die. It is a very long scripture. Do not stay to hear it through.
ucq_scarlet_pressure.turn_in_text: Good. The portal stays dark and the Crusade stays outside. The Queen will hear the road is quiet. She likes to hear it. It is one of the few things that makes her pause. Take your reward, and wash. They burn incense, and it clings.

ucq_scarlet_orders.description: Wrenfall wants to read what the Crusade has been told. The Scarlet converts and initiates carry orders in a neat red hand, copied and recopied, and a pattern is beginning to emerge. She needs five of them to piece together a picture. She says it is like reading a letter through a keyhole.
ucq_scarlet_orders.accept_text: The Crusader's Outpost, east of Brill, and the farm roads. Anyone in Scarlet who can read. Bring me five. Do not bleed on them, if you can help it. Ink and blood together are impossible to read.
ucq_scarlet_orders.turn_in_text: A very tidy hand. They are afraid of us, and have been told to hide it. I find that touching. I will pass the pattern up the line. Someone with more rank than me will know what to do with it. I expect that someone will enjoy it.

ucq_tin_bars.description: Smith Ironbrow has a bench, a quench trough, and no tin. The Undercity Forge in the War Quarter is cold because nobody has bothered to light it, and Ironbrow cannot light it himself: his hands have gone to cold iron. Smelt three tin bars and he will know the fire is yours, and so will the forge.
ucq_tin_bars.accept_text: Tin ore from the western hills if you have no stock. The forge is south-west of the War Hall. Light it, and smelt three bars. Don't rush the fire. A forge sulks if it is hurried, and a sulking forge is a long afternoon.
ucq_tin_bars.turn_in_text: Three bars, and not a cinder wasted. That is how you light a forge. My old master used to say a forge only forgives patience, and I have found it forgives very little else. Come back when you need to learn what iron is for.

ucq_iron_bars.description: With tin in hand, Ironbrow wants rough iron for the Royal Guard's greaves. The Guard have been marching in leather for a year, and a leather boot does not discourage a Scarlet sword. Smelt three rough iron bars at the Undercity Forge. He will even let you use his good tongs.
ucq_iron_bars.accept_text: Rough iron, three bars. Don't touch the tongs on the left. They bite, and not metaphorically. Keep your feet clear of the trough. The water has been hot since the Plague, and nobody remembers why.
ucq_iron_bars.turn_in_text: Rough iron, rough work. The Guard will wear them with pride, or at least with plates. Good bars, even and clean. If you ever want to make something of yourself, there is a bench here with your name on it. Quite literally. I carved it last night.

ucq_drill_remnants.description: Drillmaster Hask is running out of recruits who do not mind being hit. The Lordaeron Remnants in the Ruins above are persistent and cheerfully hostile, and it is high time somebody used them for target practice. He wants eight dropped, and four of their signets brought down to show the recruits what they fight.
ucq_drill_remnants.accept_text: North, up the shaft, then south along the road to the Ruins. Eight remnants, four signets. Pretend you are teaching them. They won't learn, but it makes the work lighter.
ucq_drill_remnants.turn_in_text: Eight and four. The recruits will learn more from your signets than from my yelling. I've never been one for kindness, but that was a clean job, and I will say so to anyone who asks. Nobody ever asks.

ucq_drill_brennic.description: Crusader Brennic holds the Scarlet outpost east of Brill. Hask has heard his name a great deal lately, usually spat. He would like the man in the pit, in a manner of speaking. The recruits need to see what a real enemy looks like when it falls.
ucq_drill_brennic.accept_text: The Crusader's Outpost. His armour is polished. His faith is brittle. Break one of them and the other will follow. Take care on the stairs. They are longer than they look.
ucq_drill_brennic.turn_in_text: Polished and brittle indeed. Take your prize and tell the recruits you did not enjoy it. They need to believe that killing is work and not pleasure. I'm half-afraid it is both. Welcome to the pit.

ucq_valdis_relics.description: Magistrix Valdis has been studying the Agamand wards, and the wards have been studying her. They are more patient than she is, and a good deal older. She needs five grave relics from the crypt-keepers in Western Tirisfal to complete her notes, and she needs them before the wards finish theirs.
ucq_valdis_relics.accept_text: The Agamand Family Crypt, Western Tirisfal. The wights and graverobbers carry the relics. Five. Do not hold them longer than you must. They have a way of remembering whose they were.
ucq_valdis_relics.turn_in_text: A ward of twelve strokes, carved by a mason who couldn't count. Delightful. Thank you. I shall try not to dream about it tonight, which is difficult for a creature that does not sleep.

ucq_kolven_ledger.description: Dreadmaster Kol'ven wants to know who the Cult of the Damned bargain with. The cultists carry ledger pages. The pages carry names. The names carry weight. He wants six, and wants them before the cult realises someone is reading its accounts.
ucq_kolven_ledger.accept_text: Cult Farm, Eastern Tirisfal. Acolytes, fanatics. Six pages. Don't read the last line of any page. Trust me. I have, and I would give a great deal to forget what I saw there.
ucq_kolven_ledger.turn_in_text: Six pages. So it isn't one of mine. Pity, I would have enjoyed the argument. I shall pass the names up the line. Whoever signed these has either been very brave or very stupid, and I am betting on the second.

ucq_marwen_sacs.description: Apothecary Marwen runs on venom, bile and spite. The Venomweb skitterers east of Brill carry sacs that clear the throat of a retort like nothing else, and her stock is down to dregs. She wants six, whole, and she wants them fast, before the dregs set.
ucq_marwen_sacs.accept_text: Venomweb Vale in Eastern Tirisfal. Sacs, not spiders. The spiders are mostly legs. Six, unbroken. If one pops, pour it into a vial and tell me. I can use that too, but I charge the difference.
ucq_marwen_sacs.turn_in_text: Fat, ripe and unburst. You have a gift. Here, for the effort. Don't tell the Society I paid you a fair rate. They expect me to haggle, and I don't want them thinking I've gone soft.

ucq_stray_vial.description: A sealed vial taken off a Plagued Courier on the Silverpine road. The Apothecary Society's wax is on the stopper, and so is a hairline crack. Master Apothecary Sable will want to know why a Society vial is running about the forest in the pocket of a courier who should not have been there.
ucq_stray_vial.accept_text: You turn the vial in the light. The wax is Society wax. The Master Apothecary's lab, in the Apothecarium, is the place for it. Hand it over, and tell her where you found it.
ucq_stray_vial.turn_in_text: The wax is ours. The compound is not on any ledger I signed. Someone has been busy behind my back. I shall find out who, and when I do, I shall be very polite about it, and then I shall be very thorough.

ucq_sennarath_scroll.description: Loremaster Sennarath has tracked the Cult's cipher across half of Lordaeron, and now believes Keeper Oswin at Raven Hill Cemetery has the missing key. The scroll is sealed in grave-wax. She is not letting it leave the Undercity except in a pair of steady hands. She has examined yours, and decided they will do.
ucq_sennarath_scroll.accept_text: North, by portal, into Silverpine. Raven Hill Cemetery. Oswin knows the cipher. Put it in his hand. Do not read it. If you hear someone behind you on the road, do not turn around. Walk faster.
ucq_sennarath_scroll.turn_in_text: He frowns the way I do. A good sign. Give me a moment, there will be a reply. He is a careful man. Careful men take a day to write a sentence and a week to forget one.

ucq_oswin_reply.description: Keeper Oswin has read Sennarath's scroll twice and written a reply. The reply is short, and clearly not meant for the road. He has given it to you folded small, wrapped in a strip of grave-linen, and asked you to take it back to Loremaster Sennarath in the Magic Quarter.
ucq_oswin_reply.accept_text: Back to the Undercity and Sennarath. Keep it dry. Keep it close. Keep your opinions to yourself. If anyone asks, you are carrying laundry.
ucq_oswin_reply.turn_in_text: "Yes, the key is in the husks." Of course it is. Oswin always did like his answers buried. Thank you. I shall have to send someone out to dig, and I have a suspicion who it will be.

ucq_groundskeeper_scrap.description: Torn from the pocket of a Skeletal Groundskeeper at Raven Hill: a fragment of ledger in the Cult's cipher. A few words, a number, a smear. Sennarath is the only person in the Undercity who might read it, and the only one who would enjoy the attempt.
ucq_groundskeeper_scrap.accept_text: You hold the scrap up to the light. Sennarath, in the Magic Quarter. She loves a scrap. She will love this one more. Don't stay for the explanation. It will take an hour.
ucq_groundskeeper_scrap.turn_in_text: A line of the cipher, in a groundskeeper's pocket. How very careless of someone. Thank you. This is exactly the missing thread. The groundskeepers did not write it, of course. Somebody has been using them as filing cabinets.

ucq_pyrewood_hunt.description: Ranger Isolde hunts what the Dark Lady needs hunted, and this season it is the worgen around Pyrewood Village: thickening in number, bolder in daylight, and very much not our friends. The Pyrewood pack has started to move in daylight, which she finds rude. She wants twelve of them gone before the next full moon.
ucq_pyrewood_hunt.accept_text: Pyrewood Village, Silverpine South. Watch the treeline. They love the treeline. Six ambushers and six ferals. Don't fight in the open. The ambushers always know where the open is.
ucq_pyrewood_hunt.turn_in_text: Twelve less to watch. The Dark Lady will hear of it, if only because I will tell her. Take your reward. And shake the fur out of your cloak before you enter the throne room. She is particular about the floors.

ucq_watchman.description: A Forsaken Watchman at Raven Hill never stopped his patrol. He no longer answers challenges, or his own name, and the groundskeepers have begun to follow him on his rounds. Deathstalker Rhyne has been asked to put him down quietly, and has decided the quiet option is you.
ucq_watchman.accept_text: Raven Hill Cemetery, Silverpine North. The groundskeepers first. They hear everything. Then the Watchman. He still wears his badge. Don't take it off him unless you have to. He's very proud of it.
ucq_watchman.turn_in_text: Quiet work. Efficient. I may recommend you to Rhyne's less dignified cousins. Take your reward. And if you find yourself walking the same road for no reason, stop and ask who ordered you to. It will save you a lot of time.

ucq_dark_ladys_ear.description: Three separate reports have reached Wrenfall: the Scarlet interrogator's ledger, the Scourge Cave's necromancer, and the Agamand cipher in Silverpine. Each is a thread. Sylvanas would like to see them tied. Whoever carried those three threads should stand in front of her. She has asked for you by description, which Wrenfall finds unsettling.
ucq_dark_ladys_ear.accept_text: The Queen is in the Royal Quarter's great hall. Stand before her. Bow, if the knees allow it. She has noticed that some of the newly woken do not answer to anyone, and she has expressed curiosity about it. Be curious back.
ucq_dark_ladys_ear.turn_in_text: She has been told. She says: "Remember the face." I would take that as the highest praise she gives. Whatever else you do, do not ask her what she meant by it. Nobody does, and nobody has lived long enough to complain.

ucq_deeps_warning.description: Gatewarden Sorrel keeps the iron door at the south end of the wheel. Nothing has come up from the Deeps for weeks, which she does not like. A quiet door is a patient door. She wants someone to stand at the gate and see whether it feels as quiet as it sounds.
ucq_deeps_warning.accept_text: Stand at the iron door in the south. Count to thirty. Tell me if you hear anything. Do not open it. If it opens by itself, do not run. Walk backward, and keep your hand on the wall.
ucq_deeps_warning.turn_in_text: You heard it too, then. Good. I was afraid I was imagining it. Come back when you are much stronger. There is work below, and it will not wait for you to feel ready.

ucq_pd_gate.description: Sorrel is no longer certain what is coming up the Deeps stair. Whatever the Society's alchemists are breeding down there is flooding the Outer Cistern with rats, worms, hounds and walking corpses. She wants the first chamber quieter, so she can open the door without wincing.
ucq_pd_gate.accept_text: Through the iron door, then down. The Outer Cistern. Bring friends. The Society's work is not for lone travellers. Eight zombies, six hounds, six worms. Do not drink the water, whatever it looks like.
ucq_pd_gate.turn_in_text: You came up with all your limbs and a better colour than most. That is progress. Sit. Tell me what you saw. I have a ledger of things that should not be down there, and I am afraid it is getting long.

ucq_pd_sump.description: Master Apothecary Lorrane Sable cannot prove it, but she suspects the sump water in the Plague Depths is carrying the plague to the Cistern's lower works. She wants six sealed vials of the sludge from the spore-things and the rot worms, to test. She says she has a feeling about the colour, and she would very much like to be wrong.
ucq_pd_sump.accept_text: The Outer Cistern. Plague Spores and Rot Worms. Six vials, stoppers on. If you drop one, don't tell me. I will smell it on you, and I would rather not have to say so.
ucq_pd_sump.turn_in_text: Six. Green-grey. Warm. Not natural, not remotely. Someone is feeding this on purpose. Thank you. I will run the assays tonight, and tomorrow I will tell you what I should have guessed a week ago.

ucq_pd_vex.description: The sludge reads like a recipe: a familiar hand, a familiar flourish. It is Vex's. The Plagueweaver of the Society's inner circle weaves the plague through the Weaving Hall's looms, and she is not working for the Dark Lady any more. Sable would rather you did not hesitate, if you meet her.
ucq_pd_vex.accept_text: The Weaving Hall, west of the Mid Conduit. She was a friend once. That is the worst of it. She will recognise you, I think. Do not let her speak first. Her voice was always her best instrument.
ucq_pd_vex.turn_in_text: Her needle. Of course. She always did sew too tightly. Thank you, and I am sorry you had to do it. I will put her name in the ledger as lost. It is not the right word. It is the only one I have.

ucq_pd_notes.description: Marwen has heard rumours that the Plague Surgeons are the Society's loyal hands, taking notes for a clinical record of the plague's progress. If there is a ledger of the spread, she wants it. Five pages from the surgeons, bloody or otherwise. She says the handwriting will tell her whether they enjoyed it.
ucq_pd_notes.accept_text: The Lab wing. Plague Surgeons. The pages are bloodied but legible. Five. Read them before you hand them over, if you like. It will do you good to know what you fought.
ucq_pd_notes.turn_in_text: Five pages. A neat hand, a steady one, and a growing unease in the last entries. We know how it spreads now. That is both the best news and the worst. Thank you. Go and get some air. Not that you need it.

ucq_pd_ledger.description: Loremaster Sennarath knows who the conspirators bribed, because the Blighted Courtiers of the Throne of Rot keep a ledger of every favour. She wants four copies of the courtier ledger from the Court, to compare against Wrenfall's lists. She says it is the closest thing the conspiracy has to a conscience.
ucq_pd_ledger.accept_text: The Court of Rot, north-west wing. The Blighted Courtiers. Four ledgers, any condition. I can read through a stain. Do not read them yourself. The sums are quite ordinary. That is what makes them terrible.
ucq_pd_ledger.turn_in_text: Names, dates, sums. Every one struck through, and every sum still correct. Terrifying and tidy. Thank you. Wrenfall will want to see these tonight, and I would not keep her waiting.

ucq_pd_noble.description: The Faulkner line was Lordaeron nobility. The last Faulkner was murdered in his bed, raised in a vat, and given a signet he does not remember. The Society dressed him as a figurehead for the coup. Wrenfall wants the figurehead removed and the signet recovered, quietly, and without a ceremony.
ucq_pd_noble.accept_text: Throne of Rot, the Plague Depths' west wing. Kill him. Take the signet off the body. Do not wear it. Not even to see how it fits. It has a way of fitting.
ucq_pd_noble.turn_in_text: A dead man's ring on a dead man's finger. Good. It goes in the vault, and the vault stays shut. He was a decent lord once, you know. I met him at a banquet. He had very good manners.

ucq_pd_voss.description: Plague Keeper Voss keeps the Archive: a thousand recipes, a thousand formulae, and the notes that tie them together. Sennarath wants the Codex, in one piece, and Voss out of the way of it. She says the Codex has no business belonging to anyone who still believes in the Society.
ucq_pd_voss.accept_text: The Blight Archive, east wing. Voss is a careful curator. Be more careful. Do not let him hand you a book. Every book he hands you is a trap, and some of them are very good traps.
ucq_pd_voss.turn_in_text: A thousand recipes, one ledger. The conspiracy is on every page. We may yet outpace it. I shall need a week, a candle, and a very strong cup of whatever the Apothecaries are calling tea this season.

ucq_pd_vats.description: Surgeon Halvard needs to see what the Society has been growing in the Vault of Flesh. The failed experiments carry fistfuls of tissue still working out what they were supposed to be. Five samples will tell him how long the vats have been running, and how many are still fed.
ucq_pd_vats.accept_text: The Vault of Flesh, east wing. Failed Experiments. Gloves on. Don't think about the faces. They are faces, though. That is the part I cannot make myself tell the Queen.
ucq_pd_vats.turn_in_text: Five. Fresh, grey and still trying. The vats have been running longer than anyone told me. I shall have words with the people who did not tell me. The words will be short and sharp, and some of them will be Latin.

ucq_pd_abomination.description: The tissue samples point to a single source: a creature at the heart of the Vault of Flesh, still growing. Halvard calls it the Vile Plague Abomination. It does not recognise anything as a friend, and it is the Society's proudest and most terrible work.
ucq_pd_abomination.accept_text: The Vault of Flesh, deepest chamber. It is large, loud and wet. Bring a healer. And a very strong stomach. When it falls, stand clear. It makes a sound as it goes.
ucq_pd_abomination.turn_in_text: Growth stopped. Marvellous and terrible. The Society should be ashamed. Take the pick of what's left. I shall take samples of my own, if you do not mind, and then I shall burn the room.

ucq_pd_zulketh.description: Vex, the Noble, Voss and the Abomination were the Society's four limbs. Zul'keth is the heart: a Dark Sorcerer who believes the Dark Lady has failed, and who has built a pulsing furnace of plague under the city to prove it. End him, and the Society's coup ends with him.
ucq_pd_zulketh.accept_text: The Plague Heart, the deepest room. Everything you have killed so far was his. Finish it. He will talk, because they always do. Don't listen. Strike when he pauses for breath, if he still breathes.
ucq_pd_zulketh.turn_in_text: It beats no more. The Society is leaderless and the Dark Lady is still on her throne. Take her gratitude, and mine. I shall sleep tonight, which I have not done in a month. If you hear snoring from the Apothecarium, that is only me.

ucq_pd_report.description: Master Apothecary Sable has written the whole sorry tale of the Society's coup into a sealed report. It needs to reach the Queen herself: not by messenger, not by raven, but by the hand that finished it. She trusts no other courier, and has said so, and has underlined it.
ucq_pd_report.accept_text: The Royal Quarter's great hall. Hand it to her. Do not say anything clever. She hates clever. She will wait for you to finish, and then she will tell you what she thinks, and you will know exactly where you stand.
ucq_pd_report.turn_in_text: She reads it, slowly. She says nothing. Then she says: "The Forsaken do not forget." That is as close to thanks as the Dark Lady gets. Take it. You will not hear it again.
